name: spid3r
description: A fast, modern programming language written in Rust with dual execution engines (Tree Interpreter & Bytecode Stack VM), gradual typing, 20+ built-in data structures, WebAssembly browser playground, desktop webview GUI, and native LLVM AOT machine-code compilation.

paragraphs: A small, dynamically typed programming language with optional static types, written in pure Rust.

Spid3r programs (.matrix files) run on two interchangeable engines — a tree-walking reference interpreter and a bytecode compiler with a stack VM — that are tested to produce identical output. The core toolchain has zero third-party dependencies.
features: Readable syntax: fn, let, const, if/elif/else, while, for … in, C-style for.
First-class functions and closures that capture their surrounding variables (both top-level and local fn declarations).
Classes and interfaces: single inheritance (extends), implements, and
public/private members (private by default, enforced at check time).
Structured errors: throw, try/catch/finally (running finally deterministically on normal exit, throw, return, break, and continue), plus option (some/none)
